title: Daily Market Digest - October 1, 2026
subtitle: Market closes mixed as surging bond yields and AI optimism create a two-tiered market.

items.headline: Wall Street finishes mixed amid bond market swings and AI-driven tech strength
items.summary: U.S. equities saw a choppy session today, October 1, 2026, as major indices reacted to surging Treasury yields hitting multi-decade highs, while optimism surrounding AI and strong earnings from tech giants provided support. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended slightly higher, breaking a three-day losing streak for the S&P, while the Dow edged down. The divergence highlights a 'two-tiered market' where growth and AI-related stocks continued to show resilience.

items.statContext: Up 0.34% today. The S&P 500 closed with a 0.19% gain. It rose 18.58 points, or 0.24%. It gained 14.91 points.
Up 0.1% today. It rose 10.53 points. Earlier, it advanced 0.44% in early trading.
Up less than 0.1% today. It edged up 3.17 points, or 0.01%. The Dow also added roughly 85 points, or 0.2% in the opening.

items.headline: Accenture Surges on Strong Earnings and Outlook
items.summary: Accenture PLC ($ACN) jumped 15.6% to $211.97 after reporting quarterly results that beat expectations and providing an upbeat fiscal 2027 outlook.

items.headline: Synopsys Climbs on Price Target Hike and Growth Outlook
items.summary: Synopsys Inc. ($SNPS) climbed 12.81% to $490.66 after KeyBanc hiked its price target to $605, citing the electronics company's fiscal 2027 outlook and long-term growth.

items.headline: Corteva Plunges Amid Broader Market Volatility
items.summary: Corteva Inc. ($CTVA) was among the session's notable decliners, sliding 84.38%.

items.headline: General Mills Hits 52-Week Low as Rising Rates Weigh on Consumer Sector
items.summary: General Mills ($GIS) hit a 52-week low, dropping 2.44%, as rising interest rates continue to pressure the consumer sector.

items.headline: Energy and Technology Lead Market Gains
items.summary: The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLE) gained 1.10%, with EOG Resources Inc ($EOG) up 2.37%, ConocoPhillips ($COP) 1.20%, and Chevron Corp ($CVX) 0.92%. Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLK) rose 0.26%, boosted by NVIDIA Corp ($NVDA) up 0.91% and Microsoft Corp ($MSFT) 0.48%. The S&P 500 energy index also saw a boost of almost 2%. Meanwhile, Utilities Select Sector SPDR ($XLU) rose 1.2%.

items.headline: Financials and Materials Lag Amid Market Volatility
items.summary: The Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLF) declined 0.90%, with Bank of America Corp ($BAC) down 2.30%, JPMorgan Chase & Co ($JPM) 1.11%, and Mastercard Inc ($MA) 0.35%. Materials Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLB) fell 1.33%, and Real Estate Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLRE) was down 0.99%. Basic materials stocks were noted as primary laggards.

items.headline: AI Optimism Fuels Tech Sector Despite Broader Concerns
items.summary: AI-related stocks, including those in the semiconductor sector, saw gains today, driven by blowout quarterly results from Micron Technology ($MU) and the introduction of Alphabet's ($GOOGL) newest Gemini model. This renewed faith in the AI trade supported Wall Street, even as some analysts noted that Micron's stock slipped despite strong results, indicating high investor expectations already priced in.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Surge to Multi-Decade Highs, Pressuring Markets
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields surged to their highest levels in over two decades, with the 10-year yield hitting an intraday high of 5.342% and the 30-year yield reaching 5.663%. This increase pressured blue-chip dividend stocks and weighed on the broader market, though yields pulled back slightly later in the day.

items.headline: Mixed Economic Data Released: Jobless Claims Fall, ISM Manufacturing Dips
items.summary: Weekly jobless claims fell to 197,000, reaching a nearly 57-year low, indicating a solid labor market. However, the ISM manufacturing index for September came in at 54.5, slightly below estimates of 54.9, and down from 54.6 in August, showing mixed signals on growth and persistent price pressures due to rising input prices.

items.headline: Fed Remains Wary of Inflation Despite Cooler PCE Data
items.summary: Despite core PCE (Personal Consumption Expenditures) inflation coming in below economists' forecasts at 3% annually, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson stated that inflation is 'still too high' and that recent data didn't significantly change his view. Expectations for the Fed to keep rates unchanged at its October meeting have increased, with markets pricing in a 62% chance of no hike.

items.headline: Key Earnings Reports Drive Stock Movements; Nike to Report After Hours
items.summary: Accenture PLC ($ACN) and Micron Technology ($MU) reported stronger-than-expected quarterly results, significantly impacting their stock prices. Accenture surged over 15%, while Micron's stock slipped despite strong performance, indicating high investor expectations. Nike ($NKE) is scheduled to report earnings after the bell today.
